request.spec:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).

agent.result_text:
Each person row now shows a `person-score` column. Three of the four tests pass; "score scenario 3" fails at a quick-add step (line 1077) that runs before any score check. It fails the same way with my change removed.

**What I added** (front end only, no server or schema change, since all the inputs were already on the client):
- `src/main/frontend/features/score/score.ts`: `personScore` adds up the due of the person's SETTLED claims that count, skipping n/a. That due comes from the same `claimDue` the due-total uses, so it is the due fixed at settlement when there is one. It takes 5 off for each overdue claim that counts, using the existing `personOverdue`. It rounds half to even using whole-number arithmetic, so no floating-point error.
- `src/main/frontend/features/score/score.slot.tsx`: a "Score" header and a `<td data-testid="person-score">` cell, placed next to the Overdue columns.

**Test results** (`PORT=3471 bin/e2e`):
- "score", "score scenario 1" and "score scenario 2" pass.
- "score scenario 3" fails at line 1077: wes, who has the "restricted" role, quick-adds a claim for a new person, Dot. The app saves it (the audit log shows `PERSON_ADDED … by=wes name=Dot` and `CLAIM_ADDED`). But the existing rule in `src/main/frontend/features/people/visible.ts` shows a restricted user only the people in their own crews. wes has no crew, so Dot's row never appears to wes and the test times out.
- The test is also self-contradictory on this: it needs Dot visible to wes right after the quick add, but later (line ~1097) expects Dot's row to be gone for wes. Nothing in the app or its docs explains that, so I left the restricted-user rule alone rather than invent behaviour for an unrelated feature.
- To check the rest of scenario 3, I ran a temporary copy that does the same quick add but finds Dot's row from another user's page. It passed every remaining step, including the score values and all the audit records. I deleted the copy afterwards; the real spec is unchanged.

**Port warning:** other sandboxes on this machine sometimes serve on port 3000. When that happened, my test runs hit another app and failed at random steps. Run `bin/e2e` with a free port, e.g. `PORT=3471 bin/e2e`.

Decision for you: if restricted users should see the people they've just quick-added until the sheet is re-loaded, I can add that to `visible.ts` and scenario 3 should then pass. It changes an existing feature, so I've left it to you.
